post.caption: Unplated white gold is faintly yellow. White gold is gold mixed with white metals such as palladium, and an 18 karat piece is 75 percent gold. So jewelers plate it with rhodium for a bright white shine. Rhodium is a silvery white metal related to platinum. William Hyde Wollaston found it in the early 1800s, and its name is Greek for rose, after the color of its salts. The plating is often about a micron thick. It wears off, so rings are often re-plated every year or two. Platinum is usually left unplated because it is naturally white. In 2021 only about 24 tonnes of rhodium were mined.
